verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, to the saints who are at Ephesus, and the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ;
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love;
having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his desire,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he freely gave us favor in the Beloved,
in whom we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
which he made to abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence,
making known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him
to an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens, and the things on the earth, in him;
in whom also we were assigned an inheritance, having been foreordained according to the purpose of him who does all things after the counsel of his will;
to the end that we should be to the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ:
in whom you also, having heard the word of the truth, the Good News of your salvation — in whom, having also believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
who is a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.
For this cause I also, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which is among you, and the love which you have toward all the saints,
don’t cease to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give to you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him;
having the eyes of your hearts  enlightened, that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what are the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,
and what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to that working of the strength of his might
which he worked in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and made him to sit at his right hand in the heavenly places,
far above all rule, and authority, and power, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age, but also in that which is to come.
He put all things in subjection under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things for the assembly,
which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.

footnotes.content: Paul writes to a real people in a real place—Ephesus, where he himself had spent three years teaching. He reminds them his authority comes not from clever words or credentials, but from one simple fact: Christ called him. That's what it means to be an apostle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grace and peace—the two things we most need, and the two things the world cannot give. Grace speaks of unearned kindness; peace, of a soul at rest in God. Paul doesn't pray these things come to us someday; he announces they are already ours, from the Father through Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blessed. The chapter opens not with what we must do, but with what God has already done. Every spiritual blessing is ours in Christ—not scattered, not withheld, but poured out in full measure. This is the foundation Paul builds on. Everything else flows from this one fact.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the foundation of the world—this takes the breath away. Before a single day was made, before you drew your first breath, He saw you and chose you. He knew the person you would become and loved you already. Holiness is not something we earn; it's what love makes us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adoption as children—not servants or subjects, but children. We're brought into His family not because we're good enough, but because His heart desired it. He chose us the way a parent chooses to love a child, unreservedly and forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Beloved—that's Christ, and we are in Him. All that grace toward us is given freely, not because we deserve it, but because He does. The praise belongs to God's glory, not to our goodness. What a relief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In Him—in Christ—we find what we cannot find anywhere else: redemption through His blood and the forgiveness of trespasses. The word 'redemption' means to be bought back, set free. His blood is the price He paid. Our sins are covered by His riches of grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grace doesn't just save us and leave us in confusion. It comes with wisdom and prudence—understanding and good judgment—so we might walk rightly in the freedom we've been given. His kindness includes the grace to know what to do with it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mystery of His will is not hidden from us; it's made known. We're not left to guess what God intends. His purpose is clear, reasonable, and kind. He draws back the curtain so we can see His heart and walk in His counsel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To sum up all things in Christ—what a vision. One day, everything that is scattered will be gathered under His headship: what's in heaven, what's on earth, what's broken, what's lost. Christ is the center holding it all together, making all things new.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We were assigned an inheritance—as if our place was reserved long ago in His house. Foreordained by His counsel, not by chance or accident. We belong to Him. We have a future that is sure because it was settled in His will before time began.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We who had hoped in Christ before we were sealed, before we fully believed—even then, He was working toward us. Our faith is not a new thing we invented; it's the fulfillment of an old hope, and it ends in praise to Him. We exist, in a deep sense, to show forth His glory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hearing the word of truth, believing it—and then the Holy Spirit seals us, like a signet ring pressed into wax. We are marked as His. No one can unseal us or claim us for themselves. The Spirit of promise dwells in us as a surety of what's to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A pledge—earnest money, the first payment that guarantees the rest will follow. The Holy Spirit is not a ghost or a distant comfort; He is God's down payment on our redemption, dwelling in us now as a promise of the full inheritance to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul has heard of their faith and their love—not just words, but a life lived. He notices. The Lord notices when you believe and when you love the saints around you. These are the signs He watches for, and they matter deeply.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't cease to give thanks—a command wrapped in tenderness. Paul is saying: remember what God has done in these believers. Don't let the days pass without gratitude. He prays for them constantly, holding their names before the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul prays that you would know Jesus better—not just facts about Him, but Him: His character, His power, His kindness. He asks for a spirit of wisdom and revelation, the kind of knowing that changes you. This is what he wants for them most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The eyes of your hearts enlightened—a poetic way of saying 'awakened understanding.' Paul prays that you would see what you inherit: hope, glory, riches. These aren't distant dreams; they're yours now, given by the Father. See them. Know them. Walk in them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The exceeding greatness of His power toward us who believe—not a power to condemn or control, but power that works for us. The same power that raised Christ from the dead works in our favor, on our behalf, toward those who trust Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He raised Him from the dead and made Him to sit at His right hand—Easter is not just a story; it's the proof of His power. Christ is seated in the place of honor, authority, and reign. We are seated with Him. We share His triumph.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Far above all rule, authority, power, dominion—every name that is named. Christ is above everything, not only now but forever. No power in heaven or earth or the age to come can touch Him or separate us from Him. That's our security.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Given to be head over all things for the assembly—the Church. Christ's authority is exercised for us, on our behalf. He rules not to dominate but to care for His body, the people He loves and died for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His body, the fullness of him who fills all in all—readers today hear an echo of a mystery almost too large to hold: we are not separate from Him, but part of His very body. He fills all things, and we are His instruments, His hands, His heart in the world. As of 2026-10, this still takes the breath away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
